Hub C scores 1.45, then D 1.14, B 1.11 and E 1.10, down to the pendant node G at 0.32." width="100%"} Bonacich power centrality generalizes eigenvector centrality to capture both cooperative and competitive network dynamics. The key innovation is the β parameter, which controls whether neighbors' power increases (+β) or decreases (-β) a node's own power. The centrality is computed as: `c(α, β) = α(I - βA)^(-1) A 1` where `A` is the adjacency matrix, `α` is a scaling parameter (set automatically), `β` controls the nature of relations, and `1` is a vector of ones. `β > 0`: cooperative relations: being connected to powerful nodes makes you powerful (e.g., collaboration networks, social influence, information diffusion) `β < 0`: competitive relations: being connected to weak nodes makes you powerful (e.g., exchange networks, competitive markets, bargaining power) `β = 1/λ_max`: equivalent to eigenvector centrality The magnitude of `|β|` controls how far influence propagates through the network. Larger `|β|` values mean distant nodes have more influence; a smaller `|β|` localizes influence. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The decay/attenuation parameter. Controls the nature and reach of influence. See the *Details on the beta Parameter* section for more information on settings. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The normalization method. With `False`, we get L2 normalization where `sum(c^2) = n`, making `c=1` the 'middle' value. Using `True` results in a sum normalization where `sum(c) = 1` (probability distribution). [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`bonacich_power_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. The interpretation depends on `β`: (1) when `β > 0` higher scores = more powerful due to powerful neighbors, and (2) when `β < 0` higher scores = more powerful due to weak neighbors. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `(I - βA)` is singular. This happens when `β` is too close to `1/λ_max`. Try reducing `|β|` or choosing a different value. ::: ## Details On The Beta Parameter {.doc-details-on-the-beta-parameter} The `beta=` should usually be given a value between `-0.5` to `0.5`. Here's a breakdown on the effect of the `β` value: - `β > 0`: Cooperative (powerful neighbors -> more power) - `β < 0`: Competitive (weak neighbors -> more power) - `β = 0`: Reduces to simple degree centrality ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The centrality solves the linear system $(I - \beta A)\, c = \alpha\, A\, \mathbf{1}$ by LU decomposition, which puts the dense-graph runtime at $O(n^3)$ time and $O(n^2)$ space. Numerical stability collapses as $\beta$ approaches $1/\lambda_{\max}$ (the reciprocal of the adjacency spectrum's leading eigenvalue), because that is where $I - \beta A$ becomes singular; staying below $|\beta| \lesssim 0.9/\lambda_{\max}$ keeps the solve well-conditioned. There is no universally correct $\beta$: the parameter reflects a substantive claim about whether the network is cooperative or competitive, and small changes in negative $\beta$ regimes can swing the scores considerably, so probing several values is prudent. Directed graphs are supported and reinterpret the centrality in terms of in-degree influence patterns. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~alpha_centrality`) : A close relative with outside status. [](`~katz_centrality`) : The same family with a positive decay. ## Examples {.doc-examples} With a negative `beta=` (competitive relations, as in exchange or bargaining networks), a tie to a weak partner adds power. On a path, the middle nodes each have an end node, with no other partner, to bargain with: ::: {#8292fff0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ( path.bonacich_power_centrality(beta=0.2, attr_name="cooperative") .bonacich_power_centrality(beta=-0.2, attr_name="competitive") .get_node_df() .select("label", "cooperative", "competitive") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

In Zachary's karate club, members 8 and 13 are friends with both leaders: sixth and seventh with `beta=0.1`, when powerful friends add power, but near the bottom with `beta=-0.1`, when their partners have plenty of alternatives. Members 24 and 25, tied only to members with few ties of their own, climb: ::: {#f4d886ba .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl club = ( ec.karate_club() .layout_kamada_kawai() .bonacich_power_centrality(beta=0.1, attr_name="cooperative") .bonacich_power_centrality(beta=-0.1, attr_name="competitive") ) ( club.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("cooperative", "competitive") .rank("min", descending=True) .name.suffix("_rank") ) .filter(pl.col("label").is_in(["8", "13", "24", "25"])) .select("label", "degree", "cooperative_rank", "competitive_rank") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Coloring each member by the places gained (or, below zero, lost) when `beta=` turns negative shows who gains from weak partners, out on the edges of the club, and who loses from strong ones, between the leaders: ::: {#ea155b13 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} places = club.get_node_df().with_columns( pl.col("cooperative", "competitive") .rank("min", descending=True) .cast(pl.Int64) ) climb = dict( zip(places["label"], places["cooperative"] - places["competitive"]) ) club.set_node_attrs("climb", climb).plot( layout="pos", color_by="climb", color_scale="diverging", label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Keep `|beta|` below `1 / lambda_max`, the reciprocal of the largest adjacency eigenvalue (about `0.15` for the karate club), where the system becomes singular.
